correctness.rationale: At an unequal boundary a,b|c,d the two exterior-bond changes are +1 for matching the adjacent interior color, -1 for matching the opposite interior color, and 0 otherwise. Strict positivity requires no -1 and at least one +1. This holds at long-long boundaries and gives exactly the stated flank and isolation rules for singletons, including the wrapped n=3 case. After removing singletons the cyclic long-domain colors form a proper coloring, counted by the trace of the kth power of the off-diagonal all-ones matrix. Each long domain and optional singleton contribute t=z²[1+(q−2)uz]/(1−z); counting configurations with a distinguished long-domain start in two ways gives the n/k factor even for rotationally symmetric words. Adding constants cancels the factors (1−z), giving the claimed two polynomials, with the first two coefficients conventionally q. The positive solution of (q−1)t=1 is simple and the consecutive support powers rule out another zero at its modulus, including the q=2 test for 1+t. Continuity of the other roots gives a uniform spectral gap for the dominant reciprocal root near u=1. Thus the logarithm of the moment generating function of the singleton count has first two derivatives of order n, with limiting mean density α′(1)/α(1); implicit differentiation and Chebyshev give the stated limit (identically zero at q=2). Independent replay: /workspace/review_reproduction.py 3, direct full-energy enumeration of 180008 configurations in the three recorded grids, and exact polynomial agreement by evaluating −zW′/W at more marks than the coefficient degree. This corroborates only the finite grids.
